newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chiyoda aims for parent current profit in 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: Chiyoda aims for parent current profit in 1998/99.

text.p: Plant engineering company Chiyoda Corp said on Tuesday that it expects to post a parent current loss in the year to March 31 and the following year, but aims for a parent current profit in 1998/99.
"We have said that we will post a parent current loss for two successive business years but we are aiming to post a profit the following year," a company spokesman said.

The company said in November it expects a parent current loss of 24 billion yen in 1996/97 against a profit of 4.61 billion yen last year, mainly due to a fall in the profitability of its overseas projects.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday morning that it expected Chiyoda to post a parent current loss of 35 billion yen this year and a loss of about 10 billion yen in 1997/98.
The Chiyoda spokesman said Nihon Keizai's figures were based on the newspaper's speculation.
Chiyoda has not unveiled a specific earnings forecast for 1997/98.
